To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we found a way to construct exact solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations by means of a simple procedure that involves a deformation of an embedding of a four-dimensional manifold into a pseudo-Euclidean space of dimension N >4.
the Einstein equations of gravitation can be solved by means of the deformation of embedding, that is, by a change of the embedding functions.

the Einstein equations in a vacuum can be written as a system of partial differential equations for the embedding functions, that the system is invariant with respect to infinitesimal deformations of the embedding, that the deformations are described by a wave equation, that the deformable embedding functions can be expanded into series with respect to a parameter $\varepsilon$, and that the wave equation is a consequence of the Einstein equations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is a gravitational wave? What are the physical and geometrical characteristics of the gravitational waves? What are the sources of the gravitational waves and how do they produce them? What are the mathematical tools to describe gravitational waves and how can we use them to solve the problems?
the following topics: (i) The embedding theory of Einstein spaces. (ii) Deformations of embeddings. (iii) Approximate gravitational waves.

the following topics: (i) Deformations of embeddings of Einstein spaces into pseudo-Euclidean ones; (ii) Approximate gravitational waves via deformations of embeddings; (iii) Exact gravitational waves via deformation of embeddings; (iv) Gravitational radiation in a non-orthonormal frame; (v) Gravitational waves and their interaction with matter; (vi) Gravitational fields of rotating sources; (vii) Gravitational lensing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gravitational waves are not only approximate but are exact in this case.
gravitational waves are a consequence of the fact that the embedding of Einstein spaces in pseudo-Euclidian spaces can be performed in many different ways.
gravitational waves are approximate, and not exact solutions of the Einstein equations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new method of constructing approximate solutions for Einstein equations in vacua.
we are able to obtain the gravitational waves in the form of a deformation of the embedding of the Einstein space.
the Einstein equations can be solved approximately by means of a deformation of the embedding functions of a given Einstein manifold, which is a global embedding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gravitational waves in the form of small deformations of embeddings are a natural and general phenomenon in Einstein gravity.
the gravitational wave solutions of the Einstein equations can be obtained by solving a system of partial differential equations of second order.
the gravitational wave solutions are characterized by the functions vA and wA, and the latter can be chosen to satisfy certain boundary conditions.
